assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Extraction
items.clue: Getting a metal out of its compound in an ore.

items.label: Polymer
items.clue: A substance made of very long chain molecules.

items.label: Reinforced concrete
items.clue: A composite building material with steel rods set inside it

items.label: Gold
items.clue: An unreactive yellow metal found in the ground as the element itself

questions.stem: In the reactivity series, where is carbon placed?

options.text: Below gold, at the bottom
Between aluminium and zinc
Above potassium, at the top
Between iron and copper

questions.explanation: Yes. Carbon sits below aluminium and above zinc. Potassium to aluminium are more reactive than carbon; zinc to gold are less reactive.

questions.stem: Copper oxide powder is heated strongly with carbon powder. What does the carbon do?

options.text: It takes the oxygen from the copper oxide
It burns to make heat that frees the copper
It joins on to the copper to make a compound
It destroys all the oxygen in the copper oxide

questions.explanation: Yes. Carbon is more reactive than copper, so it takes the oxygen and becomes carbon dioxide: copper oxide + carbon → copper + carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Which statement about materials is correct?

options.text: Metals are very good heat insulators
A kettle case is too hard to be a polymer
Ceramics are hard but can shatter
Carbon fibre is light and so it is weak

questions.explanation: Yes. Ceramics are hard and stiff, but they are brittle, so a mug or tile can crack or shatter when dropped.

questions.stem: A piece of zinc and a piece of copper are put into separate test tubes of dilute hydrochloric acid. What would you see?

options.text: Only the zinc gives bubbles
Only the copper gives bubbles
Both metals give bubbles
No bubbles on either metal

questions.explanation: Yes. Zinc is above copper in the reactivity series and reacts with the acid, so it fizzes. Copper is too unreactive to react with dilute acid.

questions.stem: In a furnace, iron oxide is heated strongly with carbon. What are the products?

options.text: Iron carbonate alone
Iron and oxygen gas
Iron and nothing else
Iron and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Yes. Carbon takes the oxygen from the iron oxide: iron oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is correct?

options.text: Tiles are so hard that they do not crack
Plastic bottles soften when heated
Foam insulates, so it stays solid in a fire
Fibreglass shatters just like glass

questions.explanation: Yes. Plastic bottles are made of a polymer, and most polymers soften or melt when heated. That is why plastic is not used for very hot jobs.

questions.stem: Which statement about the reactivity series is correct?

options.text: Iron is more reactive than sodium
Iron is more reactive than aluminium
Calcium is more reactive than iron
Copper is more reactive than carbon

questions.explanation: Yes. Calcium is near the top of the series, above carbon, while iron is below carbon, so calcium is much more reactive.

questions.stem: Lead is less reactive than iron but more reactive than copper. Which statement about getting lead from lead oxide is correct?

options.text: Carbon can extract it, as carbon extracts any metal
Carbon can extract it, as lead is below carbon
Carbon cannot extract it, as carbon is below lead
Carbon cannot extract it, as lead is unreactive

questions.explanation: Yes. Lead is below iron, so it is below carbon too. Carbon is more reactive, so it takes the oxygen: lead oxide + carbon → lead + carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: A kiln heats pottery to over 1000 °C. Which material is best for lining the inside of the kiln?

options.text: A ceramic, as it stays solid when very hot
A polymer, as it is a good heat insulator
A metal, as it is a good heat insulator
Fibreglass, as it has the properties of glass

questions.explanation: Yes. Ceramics stay solid at very high temperatures and let heat through only slowly, so they are used to line kilns and furnaces.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water. Which element reacts faster than magnesium with cold water?

options.text: Iron (Fe)
Carbon (C)
Copper (Cu)
Calcium (Ca)

questions.explanation: Yes. Calcium is above magnesium in the reactivity series, so it reacts faster: it bubbles steadily in cold water.

questions.stem: Zinc oxide is heated with carbon, and the zinc oxide is reduced. In chemistry, what does 'reduced' mean?

options.text: It has gained oxygen
It has become smaller
It has lost its oxygen
It has joined to carbon

questions.explanation: Yes. At KS3, reduction is loss of oxygen. Carbon takes the oxygen, so zinc is left.

questions.stem: Copper wires in electrical cables are coated in a polymer such as PVC. Which properties make the polymer suitable?

options.text: Flexible, and it conducts electricity well
Flexible, and a good electrical insulator
Hard and brittle, to resist scratches
Strong, with a very high melting point

questions.explanation: Polymers such as PVC are flexible and do not conduct electricity, so they make wires safe to handle.
